memory_bridge: Spread the ground into a folded map: the printed 地図 uses On チ, while unfolding it onto the actual 地面 switches the same character to On ジ. The paper and terrain scenes keep the two compound readings distinct.

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 地図（ちず）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: Draw roads across the earth and fold it into a 地図（ちず）, “map”; the first character is read On チ.

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 地面（じめん）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: Drop the map and let it land flat on 地面（じめん）, the “ground”; the first character now takes On ジ.

memory_bridge: On デン appears in agricultural compounds; Kun た is the native word for a rice field.

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 水田（すいでん）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: Water fills all four plots, making a paddy as deep as a den: den → デン in 水田（すいでん）.

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 田（た）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: Viewed from above with no compound attached, the four plots themselves are 田（た）, a rice field.

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 对不起 is a common modern anchor for this distinct reading.
readings.overlay: The hand adjusts the inch measure until it is 对—right—then the worker bows down in 对不起 to apologize; duì falls with the bow.
